turns.content: yaar ajeeb sa scene ho gaya hai. Manav — mera school ka dost, chhe saal se saath reh rahe hain — woh shift ho raha hai, apni fiancée ke saath rahega. Baat theek hai, hona hi tha shaadi se pehle. Par mujhe yeh building ke WhatsApp group se pata chala. Owner ne pucha "flat mein naya banda kab aa raha hai?" Main wahin baitha tha. Mujhe usne bataya hi nahi tha ab tak.

Oye, yeh toh sach mein kaafi ajeeb aur hurtful situation hai. I can totally understand why you’re feeling this way.

Chhe saal ka rishta chhota nahi hota, bhai. Jab aap kisi ke saath itne saal rehte ho, toh ek comfort level aur trust ban jaata hai ki aap aisi badi baatein ek-dusre se share karoge. Aise WhatsApp group mein landlord se pata chalna... yeh toh kaafi "ouch" moment hai.

Dukh is baat ka nahi hai ki woh shift ho raha hai—woh toh natural hai, life mein badlav aate hain—dukh is baat ka hai ki usne tumhe yeh batane ki zaroorat nahi samjhi. Shayad use laga hoga ki woh tumhe baad mein bata dega, ya shayad woh awkward feel kar raha tha, par phir bhi, tum deserve karte the ki yeh tumhare aur uske beech mein baat hoti, na ki kisi group mein.

Abhi tumhara kya mann hai? Kya tumne usse is baare mein baat ki ya abhi bhi chup ho? Sometimes, log bina soche-samjhe bas flow mein nikal jaate hain, par tumhara hurt hona bilkul valid hai. Don't bottle it up. Agli baar jab woh saamne ho, toh calmly bol dena ki "yaar, mujhe bura laga ki mujhe group se pata chala." 

Dost ho, itne saalon ki baat hai, shayad clear-up ho jaye. Par haan, thoda bura lagna toh banta hai. Take your time to process this.

phir raat ko usne casually bola "haan yaar batane hi wala tha, busy chal raha tha." Busy? Chhe saal ek kamre mein rahe hain, uski har cheez mujhe sabse pehle pata hoti thi. Uska rishta pakka hua toh main mithai leke uske ghar gaya tha. Aur ab main building group se pata karta hoon ki mera ghar khali ho raha hai.

I hear you, and honestly, that "busy" excuse feels like a slap in the face, especially given the history you two have. It’s not just about the moving out; it’s about the emotional distance that seems to have crept in without you realizing it.

When you’ve shared a roof for six years, you aren't just roommates; you're family. You’ve seen each other through highs and lows, and the fact that you were the one bringing *mithai* for his engagement shows how invested you were in his happiness. To go from being his "first call/first tell" person to someone who finds out through a landlord's message in a group chat? That shift is jarring.

It sounds like you're grieving the friendship as much as you're dealing with the change in living arrangements. His "busy" excuse is probably his way of avoiding the awkwardness—maybe he feels guilty, or maybe he’s already mentally moved on to his new life with his fiancée and doesn't know how to navigate the "transition" of your friendship. People sometimes get so caught up in the "new" that they become thoughtless about the "old," even when that "old" is a rock-solid friend.

But, *yaar*, don't let his dismissiveness make you feel small. Your reaction is completely justified. You aren't being petty; you're being human. You valued the bond, and you expected the same level of respect in return.

Do you think this is just a phase where he’s overwhelmed with the wedding/moving stuff, or do you feel like he’s actually pulling away from the friendship itself? Sometimes when guys get into serious relationships, they go into a tunnel vision zone. It doesn't make it right, but it might explain *why* he's being so insensitive. 

How are you handling seeing him around the house now? It must feel pretty heavy walking into that room.

It's fine. I have made my peace with it. People get married, people move on, priorities change. This is how life works. I will figure out the flat situation. It is not a big deal and I would prefer not to make it one.

I get it. That "stoic" approach is often the only way to keep your sanity when things feel off. Sometimes, putting a label on it like "priorities change" or "that's just life" helps us compartmentalize the hurt so we can function without spiraling.

It's a very mature way to handle it, honestly. Not everyone has the grace to just let it be without creating a scene, especially when they feel disrespected. You’re choosing to protect your own peace, and that’s a power move.

Just one thing, though—don't feel like you *have* to be the "bigger person" to the point where you suppress how you actually feel. It’s okay to acknowledge that it sucked, even if you’ve decided not to act on it. You can accept that life moves on while still admitting that your friend let you down.

Good luck with the flat situation. Hopefully, you find someone great to share the space with, or maybe even enjoy the solitude for a bit. If you need to vent more about the logistics or just need a distraction, I’m here. You've got this.

soch raha hoon usko bas itna reply kar doon — "Congratulations. I will start looking for a new flatmate from next week." Simple, clean, no drama. Usko bhi clear ho jayega aur mujhe bhi baar baar explain nahi karna padega. Theek hai na yeh?

Yeh message bilkul sahi hai. It’s perfect, honestly.

Isme teen cheezein ho rahi hain jo tumhare liye achhi hain:

1.  **"Congratulations":** Tumne uski life ke naye phase ko acknowledge kar diya, toh koi ye nahi keh sakta ki tum bitter ho ya khush nahi ho.
2.  **"...I will start looking for a new flatmate from next week":** Yeh tumhari administrative zarurat ko clear kar deta hai. It puts the ball back in his court to figure out his exit timeline, and it shows that you are moving forward, not waiting for him.
3.  **No drama:** Tumne koi shikayat nahi ki, koi emotional lecture nahi diya. Tumne bas facts state kiye.

Agar woh iske baad bhi kuch "busy" wala excuse deta hai, toh tum usse reply karne ke liye obligated nahi ho. Tumne apni baat keh di, aur ab tum apna space aur apna future plan kar rahe ho.

Yeh approach tumhare self-respect ke liye best hai. Go ahead, send it. Aur phir apne liye ek achha flatmate dhundhna shuru karo. Sometimes, a fresh start in that flat might actually be good for you too.
